7.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') with the detached subject pronoun hum ('they,' masculine plural). As an independent (not attached) pronoun, it serves as the subject of a clause and often lends emphasis to the ones spoken about.
7.root: — (conjunction plus pronoun; no root)

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: A present/future-tense passive verb meaning 'they are wronged, treated unjustly, dealt with unfairly.' It is the receiving end of injustice — to have one's due withheld or to be oppressed.
9.grammar: A present-tense passive verb: the yu- prefix with the inner a-vowel pattern marks 'are being done to,' and the -ūna ending marks a plural masculine subject ('they'). The full -ūna shows the base (indicative) form — an action genuinely taking place: 'they are [being] wronged.'
9.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression; putting a thing out of its place

1.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
1.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.

2.meaning: A present-tense passive verb (passive of Form I): 'is exposed / is presented / is brought before'. From a root of breadth and display, the passive means the subject is set forth and shown — laid open before view or brought up for inspection.
2.grammar: Present-tense passive verb (passive of the basic Form I عَرَضَ 'to present/display'). The yu- prefix (with its 'u' vowel) marks a third-person masculine singular subject AND the passive voice — the action is done TO the subject ('he/it is exposed'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, presenting it as a plain factual statement.
2.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — breadth, to display, present; (passive) to be set forth, exposed

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
6.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').
6.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, blaze, burning

7.meaning: A past-tense verb (Form IV) addressed to a group of males: 'you used up / squandered / made (something) go away'. From the root of going, the Form IV means to cause to depart — to dispatch and exhaust something so that it is gone.
7.grammar: Past-tense verb of the causative (Form IV) pattern (the leading hamza-a means 'to cause to…'). The ending -tum marks a second-person masculine plural subject — 'you (men/people) did this', a completed past action by a group.
7.root: ذ-ه-ب (dh-h-b) — to go, depart; (Form IV) to take/make go away, do away with

8.meaning: 'Your good things / your wholesome pleasures'. A feminine plural noun for things that are good, pure, pleasant, and lawful — the agreeable enjoyments and wholesome blessings of life — joined to the possessive 'your' (plural).
8.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun ('good things'). The -i before the pronoun is the oblique (genitive/accusative) ending that the sound feminine plural takes when it is not the subject. The attached -kum means 'your' (referring to a group), so the whole is 'your good things'.
8.root: ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b) — to be good, pure, pleasant, wholesome

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
9.root: — (particle)

10.meaning: 'Your life'. The noun 'life' — earthly living existence, the span of one's worldly life — joined to the possessive pronoun 'your' (plural).
10.grammar: A feminine noun ('life') with the possessive -kum ('your', for a group); its vowel is lengthened to -kumu to smooth the join before a following word starting with a cluster. The -i on the noun is its oblique (genitive) ending, typically marking possession ('of…') or the object of a preposition.
10.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — to live; life, being alive

11.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
11.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
11.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

12.meaning: 'And you sought enjoyment / took your pleasure / profited yourselves'. A connector joined to a past-tense Form X verb addressed to a male group; from the root of benefit and enjoyment, Form X means to seek enjoyment for oneself — to take one's fill of pleasures.
12.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. This is a past-tense verb of the seeking (Form X) pattern (the 'ista-' element conveys 'to seek … for oneself'). The ending -tum marks a second-person masculine plural subject — a completed past action by a group ('you all enjoyed').
12.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to enjoy, benefit, provide; (Form X) to seek/take enjoyment

13.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
13.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

14.meaning: So / then — the day; a connective particle joined to the noun 'the day.' It links to what precedes (drawing a consequence or sequence, 'so / then') and names the day.
14.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connector meaning 'so / then,' marking a result or sequence. al- is 'the.' The final -a is the accusative case, which often marks a direct object or, with time-words like 'day,' an adverbial sense ('on the day').

15.meaning: 'You are recompensed / repaid' — a passive verb meaning a group is given back what their deeds deserve, whether reward or penalty. The doer (the One who repays) is understood, not named.
15.grammar: A present/imperfect passive verb (form I). The tu- prefix with passive vowelling plus the -una ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject being acted upon ('you [all] are repaid'). The -una (not -u) shows the indicative mood, used for plain factual statements.
15.root: ج-ز-ى (j-z-y) — recompense, requital, repaying in kind

16.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
16.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

17.meaning: The disgrace / humiliation / abasement — a noun naming the state of being lowered and dishonoured, the opposite of honour and might. Carries the definite article 'the'.
17.grammar: A definite noun (with 'al-', 'the'). The final -i (kasra) is genitive: it marks the word as linked to a preceding preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to another noun.
17.root: ه-و-ن (h-w-n) — lowliness, disgrace, being held cheap

18.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
18.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

19.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
19.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. As the doer is built into the suffix, the verb itself is in its base past form ('you all were').
19.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

20.meaning: You act arrogantly / haughtily — to be proud, to puff oneself up, to scorn the truth and disdain to submit. The form X pattern conveys deeming oneself great and above others.
20.grammar: A present/imperfect verb (form X). The ta- prefix with the -una ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The -una ending (not -u) signals the indicative mood, used for ongoing or factual statements. Form X here carries the reflexive sense of 'consider oneself great'.
20.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, bigness; here pride and self-magnification

21.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
21.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

22.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
22.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

23.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
23.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
23.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

24.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
24.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
24.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

25.meaning: And by/with what…, and because of what… — a connective combining 'and', the preposition 'bi' ('with, by, because of'), and 'mā' ('what / that which'). Together they introduce the means or cause by which something is done.
25.grammar: A compound of particles: the conjunction wa ('and'), the preposition bi ('with, by, because of'), and the relative/indefinite mā ('what, that which'). It has no case ending of its own; the bi typically puts a following noun in the genitive, and here governs the unchanging word mā.

26.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
26.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. As the doer is built into the suffix, the verb itself is in its base past form ('you all were').
26.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

27.meaning: A present-tense verb addressed to a group: 'you act rebelliously / transgress / break away from obedience'. From a root meaning to depart from the right course, it denotes wilful disobedience — stepping outside the bounds of what is right and lawful.
27.grammar: Present-tense verb. The ta-…-ūn frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The ending -ūna is the plural indicative, presenting the action as an ongoing fact or habit ('you keep transgressing').
27.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — to depart from the right path; to transgress, rebel, defy

1.meaning: And remember / call to mind / mention — a command to bring something to mind, keep it in remembrance, or speak of it; in religious usage it carries the sense of mindful, devotional remembrance.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one male, 'remember!' / 'mention!', prefixed by 'and'. The vowelless ending (sukūn on the final r) is the normal form of a singular masculine command.
1.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

2.meaning: 'Brother (of)'. The noun 'brother' in the form it takes when bound to a following word — 'the brother of …'. Beyond literal kinship it can denote a member or kinsman of a people, one who belongs to a group as a brother belongs to a family.
2.grammar: A noun ('brother') that is one of a small set of nouns showing case with a long vowel: here the long -ā marks the accusative (e.g. as the object of a verb) AND signals that it is in construct with a following noun — 'the brother OF …', awaiting the word it is joined to.
2.root: ء-خ-و (ʾ-kh-w) — brotherhood; a brother, kinsman, fellow member

3.meaning: An active participle meaning 'one who transgresses, oversteps, goes beyond the limit'. It describes a person who exceeds proper bounds, acting in hostility or excess.
3.grammar: An active participle (doer pattern, originally ʿādiy → ʿādin), masculine singular, used as a noun/adjective. The -in ending is indefinite nunation in the genitive case — marking 'a transgressor' and the case used after prepositions or in noun-to-noun linkage.
3.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — to overstep, transgress, show enmity

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
4.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb (Form IV): 'he warned / gave warning / cautioned'. From a root of being on guard, the Form IV means to put others on notice of a coming danger or consequence, so that they may take heed and prepare.
5.grammar: Past-tense verb of the causative (Form IV) pattern (the leading hamza-a gives the sense 'to make aware / put on notice'). With no attached subject ending, it defaults to a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), describing a completed past act of warning.
5.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to vow, be wary; (Form IV) to warn, give notice of danger

6.meaning: His people / his folk — the community, nation, or kinfolk belonging to him, with the attached pronoun marking possession.
6.grammar: A noun with the accusative -a ending, the form used when the word is a direct object, followed by the possessive suffix -hu ('his,' masculine singular).
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a group that stands together, a people

7.meaning: 'By/in the sand-dunes (al-Aḥqāf)'. A preposition 'with/in/at' joined to a definite plural noun for long, curving dunes of sand — also used as the proper name of a region of such dunes.
7.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition ('in/with/at'); 'al-' is the definite article ('the'). The noun is a plural ('curving sand-dunes'). The final -i ending is genitive case, which is required here because the word follows the preposition bi-.
7.root: ح-ق-ف (ḥ-q-f) — a long, curved dune of sand; (plural) sand-dunes

8.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
8.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

9.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'passed away / went by / came to an end', here with a feminine subject. From a root of emptiness and elapsing, it describes times, peoples, or ages that have gone by and are now past and gone.
9.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it'), agreeing with a feminine noun. The following -i is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a word beginning with a cluster; the core ending is the feminine -at of completed past action.
9.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty, pass away, elapse; (of time/peoples) to be gone

10.meaning: the warnings
10.grammar: See Arabic text.

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

12.meaning: A noun meaning 'between, in the midst of, the space separating two things.' It denotes the interval or position dividing one side from another, and is regularly used to express 'between X and Y.'
12.grammar: A noun of place that functions adverbially ('between / in the midst of'). The final -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a following noun ('… between … OF …') or marks it as governed by a preposition. Here the -i shows it is bound to whatever noun follows it.

13.meaning: 'His two hands' — literally a dual 'two hands' with 'his' attached. Often used idiomatically for what lies 'in front of' or 'before' someone (i.e. between his hands).
13.grammar: The noun 'yad' (hand) in its dual form 'two hands'. The -ay ending is the dual in the genitive/accusative state (as opposed to -ā for the subject case), used after prepositions or in possessive links. The attached 'hi' means 'his' (the -i vowel of 'hi' harmonizing after the -ay). In construct, the dual's final -n drops before the pronoun.

14.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
14.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

15.meaning: A noun meaning 'behind him / his rear, his back-part' — the region or direction that is at the back of someone, paired with his attached possessor.
15.grammar: A noun of place ('behind, rear') with the attached pronoun -hi ('his / him'). The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following possessor or follows a preposition. The pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) precisely because of this preceding -i vowel.
15.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — being behind, succeeding, coming after

16.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
16.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

17.meaning: (That) you should serve and worship — to direct devotion, obedience, and humble submission to one worthy of it; the act of ʻībāda (worship) addressed to a group.
17.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb. The ta- prefix marks a 'you' subject, and the -ū ending makes it plural ('you all'). When governed by a preceding particle the form takes the subjunctive ('that you may worship'); the dropped final nūn (written ū rather than ūna) reflects that subjunctive/jussive state.

18.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
18.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
19.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

20.meaning: 'Indeed I / truly I' — an emphasis particle ('verily, indeed') that strongly affirms a statement, fused with the attached pronoun 'I.'
20.grammar: The particle inna asserts and emphasizes the statement that follows ('indeed, truly, it is certainly the case that…'). It governs its noun in the accusative; that governed noun (the ism of inna) is the attached pronoun -ī, 'I/me,' which functions as the subject of the inna-clause. The predicate then follows. So inna here takes 'I' as its accusative-governed subject.

21.meaning: I fear, I am afraid of, I stand in awe/dread — expressing the speaker's own fear, whether dread of harm or reverent awe.
21.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks the doer as 'I'. The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual state ('I fear / I am fearing').

22.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
22.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

23.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
23.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

24.meaning: a day — a day, the basic unit of daytime or a twenty-four-hour span; figuratively a time or occasion.
24.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending marks the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions or to link this noun to a preceding word ('… of a day').
24.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — a day, a span of time

25.meaning: An adjective meaning 'great', 'immense', 'mighty', or 'tremendous' — vast in size, importance, or gravity; used of things weighty and momentous.
25.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern (conveying a strong, established quality), carrying the genitive indefinite '-in' (tanwīn) ending. The genitive case typically appears after a preposition or when describing/qualifying a preceding genitive noun.
25.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense; (literally) bone, hence weightiness

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: "have you come to us?" — the question-marker "?" plus the past-tense verb "you came/arrived," with "us" as the destination.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb fronted by the interrogative particle a- ("is it that…?"). The -ta ending marks a single male "you" as the doer of the completed action; the suffix -nā is the object "us."
2.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʔ) — to come, arrive

3.meaning: A purpose-clause verb meaning roughly 'so that you might divert/turn us away (from something).' The opening lam expresses intended outcome ('in order to / so as to'), and the verb itself carries the sense of deflecting someone away from the truth or from their settled belief by means of a lie or persuasion.
3.grammar: The li- prefix is the 'lam of purpose,' marking the clause as the intended goal ('so that…'). The verb is present-tense, second-person masculine singular ('you'). Because it follows the purpose-lam, the verb takes the subjunctive: the final -a vowel on -fika is the mood-marker showing the action is hoped-for or aimed-at rather than asserted as fact. The attached -nā is the object 'us.'
3.root: أ-ف-ك (ʾ-f-k) — to turn/divert away from the truth; falsehood, lying

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

4.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

5.meaning: 'Our gods' — objects of worship, deities. The plural of 'ilāh' (a god/object of worship), with the attached ending meaning 'our.'
5.grammar: A plural noun, 'gods/deities,' with the possessive ending '-nā' ('our'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case-vowel, marking the noun as possessed by ('…of us') the attached 'our.'
5.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — to worship, deify; a god, object of worship

6.meaning: "so bring us / then bring to us" — the connective "so/then" plus the command "bring!", with "us" as the one brought to.
6.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male; the bare stem ending in -i is the imperative form ("bring!"). The suffix -nā is the object "us," and the leading fa- means "so/then," linking it as a consequence.
6.root: ا-ت-ي (ʔ-t-y) — to come; (with object) to bring

7.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
7.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

8.meaning: "you promise us / you threaten us" — the present-tense act of pledging or warning of something to come, by a single "you," with "us" as recipient.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a single "you" (male) as doer; the -u before the suffix is the indicative present (ongoing/general action). The suffix -nā is the object "us."
8.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, threaten

9.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
9.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

10.meaning: 'You (single male) were / used to be' — the past tense of 'to be', describing a past state, and often an ongoing or habitual condition in the past ('you used to…').
10.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) form of the verb 'to be'. The suffix -ta marks the subject as 'you', a single male. It states a condition that held in the past; paired with a following present-tense verb it often gives the sense 'you used to / you would (habitually)'.
10.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, becoming, coming to exist

11.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
11.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

12.meaning: The truthful ones — those who are sincere and speak the truth, whose words and deeds match reality. A plural describing people characterized by truthfulness and sincerity, prefixed with 'the.'
12.grammar: A masculine plural active participle ('the ones who are truthful') with the definite article 'the.' The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive (oblique) form: it marks the word either as an object of a verb or as following a preposition or possessive, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
12.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, telling the truth

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
2.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

3.meaning: Knowledge: sure, certain knowing — grasping a thing as it truly is. As a verbal noun it names the state or body of knowledge itself.
3.grammar: A definite noun with the prefixed article 'al-' ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being named.
3.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge

4.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
4.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').
4.root: — (adverb of place)

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: 'And I deliver/convey to you' — a verb of carrying a message all the way to its hearers so that it fully reaches them. The doubled middle consonant gives it the sense of conveying thoroughly and completely, as a messenger transmits what he has been entrusted with.
6.grammar: The wa- prefix is 'and.' The u- prefix marks first-person singular ('I') on this present-tense verb, and the doubled ('shadda') middle root letter makes it intensive/causative — 'cause to reach,' i.e. convey. The final -u ending is the indicative mood, presenting the action as an ongoing or habitual fact ('I do convey'). The attached -kum is the plural object 'you (all).'
6.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, arrive at, attain; to convey a message

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: I have been sent — I was dispatched or commissioned (as a messenger) by someone with a message or task.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice of the causative form ('to be made to go, to be sent'). The attached -tu marks the subject as 'I'. Being passive, the doer is unstated, and the focus is on the one sent: 'I have been sent'.
8.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; whence 'messenger' (rasūl)

9.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
9.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

10.meaning: "And yet I… / But as for me…" — a compound joining the conjunction 'and' to the contrastive particle 'but/however' (which corrects or counters a preceding statement), ending in an attached 'I'. It strongly draws attention to the speaker's own contrasting position.
10.grammar: A conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lākinna, a particle of correction that contradicts what came before. Like inna, lākinna governs the following noun or pronoun in the accusative (naṣb) and places emphasis on it; the doubled 'n' carries that emphasis. The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun, here in its accusative position as the noun of lākinna, so the whole reads an emphatic 'and yet as for me'.

11.meaning: A past-tense verb from the root of seeing, in the causative sense 'he showed / let you see / made you behold' something. So: 'he caused you (plural) to see'.
11.grammar: A perfect (past) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the causative (Form IV) pattern ('to make someone see' = to show). The final long vowel of the stem is a weak (defective) root letter. The attached -kum is the object 'you all'.
11.root: ر-ء-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see; (causative) to show, cause to behold

12.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
12.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
12.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

13.meaning: You act ignorantly; you behave foolishly without knowledge. The verb conveys being or acting in ignorance — lacking knowledge and behaving rashly because of it.
13.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb. The ta- prefix here marks a second-person addressee, and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'you (all)' in the indicative mood, indicating a real, ongoing action. The full -ūna (not shortened to -ū) shows the verb stands free of any particle that would cut it short.

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they saw it' / 'they perceived it' (with an object 'it'). The base sense is seeing with the eyes, and by extension recognizing or witnessing something. Depending on context this form can read as a completed past act ('they saw it') or, after a conditional particle, as a prospective 'when/if they (will) see it'. The attached object pronoun makes it 'they saw/see IT'.
2.grammar: A perfect (past-form) verb. The -aw ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject: 'they' performed the act of seeing. The attached -hu is an object pronoun, 'it/him', the thing seen. While the perfect form is by default past, after a conditional particle it can carry a future/prospective force ('when/if they see it'), so the whole signals a completed — or conditionally anticipated — act of seeing by a male/mixed group upon a single object.
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, behold

3.meaning: A passing thing that shows up across the horizon — most often a cloud-bank or weather front that 'presents itself' broadside in the sky. The word names something that appears transversely and is, by its nature, transient and on the move.
3.grammar: This is an active participle on the faaʿil (فَاعِل) pattern — 'a thing that presents itself across.' The final -an is the accusative case with nunation (tanwin): nunation marks the noun as indefinite ('a/some ___'), and the accusative typically marks a direct object or a descriptive/circumstantial role within a sentence.
3.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — breadth, to present/appear broadside, to cross or come up

4.meaning: An active participle meaning 'facing / heading toward / coming up to meet' something. It pictures one thing advancing directly opposite another, on a course to meet it head-on.
4.grammar: An active participle of the 'istafʿala' (form X) pattern, prefixed mus-ta-, which here gives the sense of orienting oneself toward and advancing to meet. The final -a is the accusative case; with no nunation it signals the word is bound to a following noun (i.e. 'facing/heading toward [the …]').
4.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — front, facing, to come toward, to receive/accept

5.meaning: 'Their valleys' — the plural of a watercourse or valley-bed (a wadi), the low ground between hills along which rain-water and floods naturally run, here possessed by 'them.'
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of wadi, 'valley'; its stem is awdiyat-, ending in a tāʾ marbuta that belongs to the plural form itself, not an added suffix. The kasra (the -i vowel) sitting on that tāʾ is the genitive case-marker: the genitive appears because the noun is possessed ('the valleys OF …') or governed by a preceding word, the case English renders with 'of' or with a possessor. The attached -him is 'their.' (The vowel of the possessor is -him rather than -hum because it harmonizes with the preceding -i sound.)
5.root: و-د-ي (w-d-y) — a valley, watercourse, the bed where water flows

6.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
6.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

7.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
7.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

8.meaning: A passing thing that shows up across the horizon — typically a cloud-bank or weather front 'presenting itself' broadside in the sky. The word names something that appears transversely and is inherently transient and moving.
8.grammar: An active participle on the faaʿil (فَاعِل) pattern — 'a thing that presents itself across.' The final -un is the nominative case with nunation (tanwin): nunation marks it as indefinite ('a/some ___'), and the nominative is the case used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun standing on its own as 'it is a ___.'
8.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — breadth, to present/appear broadside, to cross or come up

9.meaning: An active participle meaning 'one that brings/sends rain upon us' — describing a cloud or sky as rain-bearing, on the point of pouring down. The causative pattern gives 'rain-giving' rather than merely 'raining.'
9.grammar: An active participle of the 'afʿala' (form IV) causative, prefixed mu-, so it means 'one that causes rain (to fall)'; form IV adds the causative sense through the prefix, with no doubled consonant. The -u ending is nominative, the case for a subject or for a predicate noun ('[it is] a rain-bringer'). The attached -nā ('us') is the object the rain is brought upon. A participle like this can govern an object just as a verb does.
9.root: م-ط-ر (m-ṭ-r) — rain, to rain, to send down rain

10.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
10.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

11.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
11.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

12.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

13.meaning: 'You sought to hasten / asked for (it) to be brought on quickly' — a verb in which one impatiently demands that something arrive sooner than its due time. The form adds the nuance of actively seeking-out speed, not merely being quick.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb of the 'istafʿala' (form X) pattern, whose ista- prefix means 'to seek/ask for' the action — here 'to seek the hastening of, to demand it be rushed.' The suffix -tum is the subject-marker for second-person masculine plural in the past tense: 'you (all) did [it].' The opening alif is a helping vowel (hamzat al-waṣl) that lets the word begin.
13.root: ع-ج-ل (ʿ-j-l) — haste, to hurry, to bring forward in time

14.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
14.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

15.meaning: A wind — a current of moving air, a gust or breeze. The same base noun for wind, here standing on its own as an indefinite subject. Grammatically the noun is feminine.
15.grammar: A noun with the ending -un: the -u is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence (the one doing or being something), and the final -n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a wind'). The noun rīḥ is grammatically feminine.

16.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
16.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

17.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
17.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

18.meaning: Painful, agonizing, deeply hurtful. An intensive adjective describing something that inflicts severe, grievous pain.
18.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl, conveying a strong, abiding quality ('truly painful'). The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the nominative case (the case of a subject or of a noun's basic naming form), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.

1.meaning: 'It utterly destroys / lays waste to' — a present-tense verb of total, sweeping demolition. The doubled middle consonant intensifies it: not just damaging but annihilating thing after thing completely.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb on the 'faʿʿala' (form II) pattern; the doubled middle root letter makes it intensive — destroying thoroughly and repeatedly. The tu- prefix here marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it/she does'), fitting a grammatically feminine doer. The final -u is the indicative mood, stating the action as an ongoing fact.

2.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
2.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.
2.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — wholeness, totality

3.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
3.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
3.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

4.meaning: By/with the command, order, or affair; conveys both a directive that must be obeyed and, more broadly, a matter or decree under someone's authority. Often denotes a divine decree or directive.
4.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'by, with, through'. The noun 'amr means a command or a matter/affair. The -i ending is genitive, which is required after a preposition and also typically links the word to a following noun ('command OF ...').
4.root: ء-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — commanding, ordering; matter, affair

5.meaning: Its Lord — 'Lord' (Rabb) denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and brings a thing to its full development; here joined to a feminine possessor.
5.grammar: A noun ending in the genitive -i, the case that typically links a word to a following noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. The attached -hā means 'its' (referring to a feminine noun). So: 'of its Lord' / 'its Lord's'.
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

6.meaning: "And they came to be / and they became," from a verb that originally means "to enter upon the morning" and by extension "to end up in a certain state / to become." It describes a group transitioning into a new condition.
6.grammar: The "fa-" prefix means "so" or "and then," marking a result or sequence. The verb is in the completed (past) tense; the "-ū" ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they"). As one of the "sisters of kāna," this verb links a subject to a predicate state, hence "they became (something)."
6.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning / the coming of daybreak; by extension, to come to be in a state

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: 'Is seen / can be seen' — a passive present-tense verb meaning that something is visible or comes into view to onlookers, without naming who does the seeing.
8.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular ('it is seen'). The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive — the subject is the thing seen, not the seer. The root's final weak letter shows up as the long -ā ending rather than a short case-vowel; in this weak verb that -ā stands in for the indicative, presenting the visibility as a present, ongoing fact.
8.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, to perceive with the eye, to behold

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
9.root: — (particle)

10.meaning: (are) their dwellings / their homes. Refers to the houses and settlements left behind by destroyed peoples — empty ruins.

parts.en: dwellings, homes, settlements (nominative broken plural construct)

10.grammar: Broken plural of maskan ('dwelling'), nominative case (marfūʿ), -u (ḍamma) ending, in iḍāfa with -hum ('their').
10.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to dwell, to settle; maskan: dwelling, home

11.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
11.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
11.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

12.meaning: 'We reward / We requite' — to repay or recompense someone for their deeds, whether with good or with due consequence.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'na-' prefix means 'we'. The stem ends in a long '-ī' (a weak final root letter); in the plain indicative this final '-ī' is what is heard, giving 'we reward'.
12.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to repay, to recompense, to requite

13.meaning: the people / the folk — a body of people, a community or group regarded collectively (here in the accusative form).
13.grammar: The l- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The final -a ending is accusative. Since the verb it follows is passive (and so takes no direct object), this accusative is adverbial — marking the circumstance or setting of the action ('before / in front of the people') rather than a thing being acted upon.
13.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to arise; a people standing together

14.meaning: 'The criminals / evildoers' — those who commit crimes and sins, the guilty who cut themselves off through wrongdoing.
14.grammar: The al- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The stem mujrim is an active participle ('one who commits crime/sin'). The ending -īna is the masculine plural marker used when the noun is in the genitive or accusative case, giving 'the criminals'.
14.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — committing a crime or sin, guilt

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: 'We firmly established them / gave them a secure footing and power' — a past-tense verb in which Allah grants a people stability, authority, and the means to prosper in the land. The doubled consonant conveys settling them in solidly.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb on the intensive 'faʿʿala' (form II) pattern (doubled middle letter), giving the sense of 'set firmly in place, empower.' The -nā suffix is the subject 'we' in the past tense (the royal/divine 'We'). The attached -hum is the object 'them.'
2.root: م-ك-ن (m-k-n) — place, standing, firmness; to establish, to empower

3.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
3.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

4.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
4.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

5.meaning: 'We firmly established you / gave you a secure footing and power' — the same act of granting stability, authority, and resources, directed at 'you (all).'
5.grammar: A past-tense verb on the intensive 'faʿʿala' (form II) pattern (doubled middle letter): 'set firmly in place, empower.' The -nā suffix is the subject 'we' in the past tense (the royal/divine 'We'). The attached -kum is the plural object 'you (all).'
5.root: م-ك-ن (m-k-n) — place, standing, firmness; to establish, to empower

6.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

7.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'We made / appointed / rendered.' This very common verb can mean to create or place something, or to assign something a state or role (to make X into Y).
7.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers. The verb often takes two objects, meaning 'to make/turn one thing into another.'
7.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

8.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
8.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

9.meaning: The faculty of hearing — the sense by which sound is perceived. As a single (collective) noun it covers the whole capacity to hear, what the ear receives. By extension it implies attentive listening, not just physical sound-reception.
9.grammar: A verbal noun naming the act/faculty of hearing. The final -an is the accusative case with nunation (tanwin): nunation marks it indefinite ('hearing, a power of hearing'), and the accusative is the case for a direct object — fitting a thing given or granted to someone.
9.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear, to listen; the faculty of hearing

10.meaning: 'And eyesight / faculties of sight' — the plural of baṣar, the power of seeing and visual perception. The plural points to organs or instances of sight (eyes / sights) rather than vision as a single mass.
10.grammar: The wa- prefix is 'and.' Abṣār is a broken (irregular) plural of baṣar, 'sight.' The final -an is the accusative case with nunation (tanwin): nunation marks it indefinite, and the accusative is the case for a direct object — fitting something given or granted.
10.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — sight, vision, insight; to see, to perceive

11.meaning: 'And hearts / inner faculties of understanding' — the plural of fuʾad, the heart understood as the seat of feeling, awareness, and comprehension (the 'inner organ' of grasping things), not the physical pump.
11.grammar: The wa- prefix is 'and.' Afʾida is a broken (irregular) plural of fuʾad, 'heart'; its stem is afʾidat-, and the tāʾ marbuta is part of that plural form, not an added feminine suffix. The final -an is the accusative case with nunation (tanwin): nunation marks it indefinite, and the accusative is the case for a direct object — fitting something given or granted.
11.root: ف-أ-د (f-ʾ-d) — the heart as seat of awareness, feeling, and understanding

12.meaning: A two-part expression meaning 'so/then what…'. It joins the connector 'so/then' with mā, a word that can ask 'what?' or function in exclamation ('how…!'), often expressing wonder or amazement.
12.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connecting particle ('so/then'). mā is an unchanging particle/pronoun used for questions ('what?') or exclamations ('how…!'); it has no case ending and stays the same in every position.

13.meaning: It availed / enriched / sufficed: a completed-action verb meaning something was of use or benefit, made one independent of need, or warded off a want.
13.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in Form IV, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The Form IV pattern is causative, giving the sense of 'making free of need' or 'being of avail.' The final long -ā is the verb's weak (defective) ending.
13.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, self-sufficient

14.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
14.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

15.meaning: 'Their hearing' — the faculty of hearing (what the ears receive, and attentive listening) belonging to 'them.'
15.grammar: A verbal noun naming the faculty of hearing, with the possessor -hum ('their') attached. The -u ending is the nominative case, the case used when the noun is the subject of a sentence (the thing doing or being something).
15.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear, to listen; the faculty of hearing

16.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
16.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

17.meaning: Their eyes / their sights: the organs of sight, or by extension acts of seeing and glances. The plural noun denotes eyes belonging to a group.
17.grammar: A plural noun (plural of baṣar, 'sight/eye') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u is the nominative ending, marking it typically as the subject; the suffix -hum means 'their' (masculine plural).

18.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
18.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

19.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the inner faculties of feeling, awareness, and understanding (plural of fuʾad) belonging to 'them.'
19.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of fuʾad, 'heart'; its stem is afʾidat-, and the tāʾ marbuta belongs to that plural form rather than being a separate feminine suffix. The -u vowel that follows the stem is the nominative case-marker, the case used when the noun is the subject of a sentence (the thing doing or being something). The attached -hum is 'their.'
19.root: ف-أ-د (f-ʾ-d) — the heart as seat of awareness, feeling, and understanding

20.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
20.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

21.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
21.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
21.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

22.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
22.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

23.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
23.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
23.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

24.meaning: A verb meaning 'they knowingly reject / deny / repudiate.' Its distinctive sense is denying something one inwardly recognizes to be true — rejection against better knowledge.

parts.en: they (the prefix marking a third-person subject)
plural marker, with the -na of the ongoing/present

24.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks 'they,' and -ūna marks a plural subject and an ongoing or repeated action. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative mood, the verb's default unbroken form.
24.root: ج-ح-د (j-ḥ-d) — to deny or reject what one knows to be true

25.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
25.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
25.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

26.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
26.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

27.meaning: And it closed in / encompassed — to surround completely and descend upon, especially of a punishment or consequence that envelops people and leaves no escape.
27.grammar: A past-tense verb (a hollow root, whose middle letter appears as the long 'ā'). It is third-person masculine singular ('he/it did') and complete in the past; it characteristically governs a following 'with/upon' to name those whom the encirclement befalls. The prefixed wa- simply means 'and.'

28.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
28.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

29.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
29.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

30.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
30.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
30.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

31.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
31.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

32.meaning: To mock, ridicule, scoff at, or deride — to treat something with derision and make light of it. The form conveys a sustained or repeated attitude of scornful jesting.
32.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb of the Form X pattern (the 'sta-' element, here seeking/intensifying the sense of mockery). The 'ya-…-ūna' frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject — 'they' do or are doing the action. The '-ūna' ending signals the plural 'they' and that the verb is in its full (indicative) form, real and ongoing.

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: 'We destroyed / We caused to perish' — to bring about ruin, annihilation, or downfall. Combines the verb 'to destroy / cause to perish' with the subject 'we'.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The attached '-nā' ending is the subject 'we' — it marks the doers of the action as a group including the speaker, with the action completed and in the past.
2.root: ه-ل-ك (h-l-k) — to perish, be destroyed; (causative) to destroy

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: Around you / in your surroundings — the area encircling or in the vicinity of the addressees. The base word means 'around/about', joined to 'you (plural)'.
4.grammar: An adverb of place, 'around/surrounding', fixed in the accusative form (the -a after ḥawl). The attached -kum addresses a group ('you all'), yielding 'around you'.
4.root: ح-و-ل (ḥ-w-l) — to surround, encircle; turning about

5.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
5.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

6.meaning: 'the towns / settlements'. The plural of qarya, a town, village, or settled habitation — any gathered dwelling-place of people.
6.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of qarya. It ends in a 'restricted' final long vowel written as alif maqṣūra (ى), which stays the same in all cases — its case is understood from context rather than shown by a changing vowel. The prefixed al- makes it definite ('the towns').
6.root: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — to gather; a gathering-place, town/settlement

7.meaning: And We distributed, varied, and laid out in diverse forms — to turn a matter over and present it in many ways, repeating and varying it so it is fully made clear.
7.grammar: An intensive past-tense verb (the doubled middle root letter gives the sense of doing thoroughly or repeatedly) prefixed with 'and'. The suffix -nā marks a first-person plural subject ('we did …').
7.root: ص-ر-ف (ṣ-r-f) — to turn, divert, vary; hence to set forth in changing, diverse forms

8.meaning: 'The signs / the verses' — the plural of 'sign,' referring to clear indicators, proofs, miracles, or the verses of revelation that point to truth.
8.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the signs'), made definite by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The sound feminine plural takes the -i ending when it is an object of a verb or linked after a preposition or possessor — that is, when it is grammatically governed rather than serving as the subject.
8.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token

9.meaning: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

9.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.
9.root: — (particle with pronoun; no root)

10.meaning: To return, go back, or turn back — to come back to a place, state, or point of origin. Used of a group: 'they return / come back'.
10.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they return'). The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks an ongoing or repeated action by a group of males or a mixed group. The -ūna 'indicative' ending appears when nothing precedes the verb to shorten it.
10.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — returning, going back, repetition

1.meaning: "So if not / then were it not for" — combines 'so/then' with 'lawlā', which introduces a 'were it not for…' condition (something whose absence would change the outcome) and can also urge 'why not…?'.

parts.en: were it not for / why not

1.grammar: A connective 'fa' ('so, then', often marking a result) plus the particle 'lawlā'. As a conditional particle 'lawlā' sets up 'were it not for X (then Y would not be)'; as an incitement it means 'why do you not…?'. It is a function word, not inflected.

2.meaning: 'He helped them / came to their aid' — a past-tense verb of giving support and victory to someone, standing by them and granting them the upper hand against an adversary. The verb form by itself names a single male doer.
2.grammar: A plain past-tense verb (form I), third-person masculine singular ('he helped, gave victory to'); with no plural suffix on the verb, the doer is grammatically one male, and any larger subject would have to be named separately. The attached -hum is the object 'them.' The final -u is a connecting vowel added to the pronoun (so it reads -humu) to ease pronunciation before the next word — it is not a case-ending.
2.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — help, support, victory; to aid, to make victorious

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: Past-tense verb (reflexive form), third person plural: 'they took for themselves, adopted, chose.' A completed act of taking something on as one's own.
4.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb in a reflexive pattern (taking something for oneself). The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural). The opening 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the cluster of consonants be pronounced.
4.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
6.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
6.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: 'An offering / a sacrifice; that which is offered to draw near'. The noun qurbān denotes something presented to Allah as a means of seeking closeness to Him.
8.grammar: An indefinite noun. The final -an is nunation in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as a direct object (the thing offered or presented).
8.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — nearness; that which brings one near

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'gods / deities' — the plural of ilāh, objects taken as worthy of worship besides Allah. It denotes claimed divine beings in general.
9.grammar: A plural noun, indefinite ('gods'), in the accusative case marked by tanwīn. The word ends in a tā' marbūṭah, which is normally silent in pause but is pronounced as -t- when a case-vowel and tanwīn follow it; combined with the accusative tanwīn this is sounded as -tan, so the full ending is ālihatan (not a bare -an). The accusative typically marks a noun as the object of a verb or the focus of certain particles.
9.root: ا-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

10.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
10.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

11.meaning: 'they went astray / erred' — to lose the right way, to wander off into error or misguidance.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -ū ending meaning 'they' (masculine plural). It conveys a completed action: 'they went astray / erred.'
11.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, lose the way, go astray
